sentences.text:
2024
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.15429 of 2018
Order:

This Writ petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India, seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a proper writ order or orders particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in trying to dispossess the petitioner from his property to an extent of Ac.0-10 guntas in Survey No.148 situated at Ghanpur Village, Nangunoor Mandal, Siddipet District for the purpose of laying C.C. Road without prior notice and without acquiring the property by adopting procedure contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act
is arbitrary and illegal against the principles of natural justice and also depriving property rights of the petitioner guaranteed under Article 300A of Constitution of India and to pass..."

2. Heard both sides and perused the entire material on record.
3.

Learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the owner and possessor of the land in Survey No.148 to an extent of Ac.0-10 guntas situated at Ghanpur Village of Nangunoor Mandal, Siddipet District.
In the subject property, the petitioner has constructed a house and living there along with family and paying property tax.

::2 : :
While it being so, the respondent No.8, who is the contractor executing the work under MLA Quota came to the village of the petitioner and started measuring and putting marks for laying the road.
In view of the same, the petitioner has asked about the sanctioned plan along with permission for laying of the said road, upon which the respondent No.8-contractor did not show any sanctioned plan.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that aggrieved by the action of the respondent No.8- contractor, the petitioner approached the Panchayat Raj Department and requested not to lay the road without acquiring the land of the petitioner under the Land Acquisition Act, 2013.

In view of the same, the respondent No.6-Assistant Executive Engineer issued a letter dated 17.03.2018 to the respondent No.8-Contractor and directed him not to lay road and stop all works until further clearance given by the Revenue Department.

In the meanwhile, the petitioner has applied for information with regard to laying of C.C. Road in the land of the petitioner ::3::

sentences.text: In spite of letter dated 17.03.2018 and pending of the letter under RTI Act, the respondent No.8-contractor has trying to lay the road in the land of the petitioner without there being any sanctioned plan and without there being any land acquisition proceedings is illegal and arbitrary.
The petitioner has filed the instant Writ Petition to direct the respondents not to acquire the land of the petitioner without following due process of law.

5. Learned Standing Counsel for Gram Panchayat appearing for the respondents,
basing on the Para No.6 of the counter affidavit filed by the respondent No.7-Gram Panchayat, would submit that the C.C road was laid on the existing gravel road and when the petitioner objected the Village Revenue Officer, enquired into the matter and submitted a report to the respondent No.3 stating that there is an existing road from Khatha road to the house of Kammarajula Shivaiah and other houses and also prior to sixteen years, the gravel road was laid on the existing road under the scheme of food for work.

The subject area is ::4::
within the Grama kantam where several houses are in existence and people residing and as per his enquiry, the C.C road has been laid on the existing road only.
6.

Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Panchayat Raj and Rural Development appearing for the respondents, basing on the Para No.3 of the counter affidavit filed by the respondent No.6-Assistant Executive Engineer, would submit that the C.C road work is undertaken under 14th finance funds but not under the MLA Quota as alleged by the petitioner.

This is an existing earthen road since from the constructions of the houses of the habitants but the same have been upgraded from earthen to C.C road and the respondents are taking up ungradation work of existing road
. He further submits that the road in question was already laid in the last week of March, 2018 before interim orders passed by this Court on 27.04.2018.
In view of the same, requested this Court to dismiss the writ petition.

7. After hearing both sides and on perusing the entire material on record, this Court is of the considered view that ::5::
the petitioner is the owner and possessor of the land in Survey No.148 to an extent of Ac.0-10 guntas situated at Ghanpur Village.

While it stood thus, the respondent- authorities are trying to lay the C.C road by occupying the land of the petitioner without issuing any notice or initiating land acquisition proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text:
8. Basing on the counters filed by the respondent- authorities, it is made clear that the respondents have already laid the C.C road in the existing road,
which was existed since long back.

2 9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the submissions made by the both sides, the Writ Petition is disposed of granting liberty to the petitioner to make a proper application for survey of his land and after conducting the said survey, if it is found that the respondent-authorities had acquired the land of the petitioner, he can approach the appropriate authorities for ::6::
land acquisition compensation.

There shall be no order as to costs.
10.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE K.SARATH Dated:03.10.2024.
